shapes.alt: Eight annual observations from 2012 to 2019 with fitted power, exponential and quartic curves. The final observation is 57.5 million.

transcription.tex: The power model estimates $16.8$ million views in 2019. The observed figure is $57.5$ million.\par The exponential model gives about $66.0$ million. The quartic curve follows the later observations closely. A close fit over these years does not establish future growth.
Question 3

The scatter diagram shows the relationship between two sets of coded data, $X$ and $Y$, where $X=\log x$ and $Y=\log y$. The regression line of $Y$ on $X$ is shown, and passes through the points $(0,172)$ and $(23,109)$.\par The relationship between the original data sets is modelled by an equation of the form $y=ax^n$.\par Find, correct to 3 decimal places, the values of $a$ and $n$.

shapes.alt: Scatter diagram of the coded data. The downward regression line passes through (0,172) and (23,109).

transcription.tex: $\log y=\log a+n\log x$. Hence $Y=\log a+nX$.\par At $X=0$, $Y=172$, so $\log a=172$ and $a=10^{172}$ exactly.\par The slope is $n=\dfrac{109-172}{23-0}=-\dfrac{63}{23}\approx-2.739$.
Question 5

The time, $t$ ms, needed for a computer algorithm to determine whether a number, $n$, is prime is recorded for different values of $n$. A scatter graph of $t$ against $n$ is drawn.\par (a) Explain why a model of the form $t=a+bn$ is unlikely to fit these data.\par The data are coded using the changes of variable $y=\log t$ and $x=\log n$. The regression line of $y$ on $x$ is found to be $y=-0.301+0.6x$.\par (b) Find an equation for $t$ in terms of $n$, giving your answer in the form $t=an^k$, where $a$ and $k$ are constants to be found.

shapes.alt: Scatter diagram of time against n. The plotted crosses rise along a curve with decreasing slope.

transcription.tex: (a) A linear model has constant slope. The points rise along a curve whose slope decreases as $n$ increases.\par (b) $\log t=-0.301+0.6\log n$.\par $t=10^{-0.301}\times10^{0.6\log n}$\par $\phantom{t}=10^{-0.301}\times10^{\log(n^{0.6})}$\par $\phantom{t}=10^{-0.301}n^{0.6}$. Hence $a\approx0.500$ and $k=0.6$.
Question 6

Data are collected on the number of units (c) of a catalyst added to a chemical process, and the rate of reaction (r). The data are coded using $x=\log c$ and $y=\log r$. It is found that a linear relationship exists between x and y and that the equation of the regression line of y on x is $y=1.31x-0.41$. Use this equation to determine an expression for r in terms of c.
Question 7

The heights, h cm, and masses, $m$ kg, of a sample of Galapagos penguins are recorded. The data are coded using $y=\log m$ and $x=\log h$ and it is found that a linear relationship exists between x and y. The equation of the regression line of y on x is $y=0.0023+1.8x$. Find an equation to describe the relationship between m and h, giving your answer in the form $m=ah^n$, where a and n are constants to be found.

The product moment correlation coefficient (PMCC), denoted by
, describes the linear correlation between two variables. It can take values between -1 and 1.
Note that PMCC is only applicable for a
correlation, i.e. closeness of fit to a linear regression line (i.e. a
‘line of best fit’). It may be the data exhibits strong correlation with respect to a different model (e.g. exponential) even when the PMCC is low.

Question 5

The width, $w$ cm, and the mass, m grams, of snowballs are measured. The table below shows the data. \par $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline\text{Width, }w&3&4&6&8&11\\\hline\text{Mass, }m&23&40&80&147&265\\\hline \log{w}&{}&{}&{}&{}&{}\\\hline \log{m}&{}&{}&{}&{}&{}\\\hline\end{array}$\par The data are coded using $x=\log w$ and $y=\log m$.\par (a) Copy and complete the table showing the values of $\log w$ and $\log m$. (3 marks)\par (b) Calculate the product moment correlation coefficient for the coded data. (1 mark)\par (c) With reference to your answer to b, state whether a model in the form $y=kx^n$ where k and n are constants is a good fit for these data. (2 marks)\par (d) Determine the values of k and n. (3 marks)
(c) The coded data lie close to a straight line since \(r\) is close to 1. A power model \(m=kw^n\) fits well.
Question 6

Question 7

From the large data set, the daily total rainfall, x mm, and the daily total sunshine, y hours, were recorded for Camborne on seven consecutive days in May 2015. \par $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline\text{Rainfall, }x&2.2&\mathrm{tr}&1.4&4.4&\mathrm{tr}&0.2&0.6\\\hline\text{Sunshine, }y&5.2&7.7&5.6&0.3&5.1&0.1&8.9\\\hline\end{array}$\par © Crown Copyright Met Office\par (a) State the meaning of 'tr' in the table above. (1 mark)\par (b) Calculate the product moment correlation coefficient for these 7 days, stating clearly how you deal with the entries marked 'tr'. (2 marks)\par (c) With reference to your answer to part b, comment on the suitability of a linear regression model for these data. (2 marks)
(a) A trace is a small amount of rainfall.
(b) Treat traces as zero. \(r=-0.473\) (3 s.f.).
(c) The negative correlation is weak. Other variables may affect the relationship, or a different model may fit better.

A spreadsheet independently generates Maths and English marks.
What is the observed PMCC between Maths and English in this sample?
What is the underlying population PMCC?
. The two sets of marks were generated independently. A random sample’s correlation may differ from the population correlation, just as a few rolls of a fair die need not show equal frequencies.
(i.e. English/Maths marks have no underlying correlation), the observed PMCC for the sample,
, could vary, and might, purely by chance, suggest some correlation. In the first sample, this happened to be positive, in the latter, negative.
If we increased the sample size (in this case 10), we’d expect the observed PMCC to more closely match the true PMCC (0).
A natural question we might therefore ask is, if we had no knowledge about the underlying population: “
statistically significant, or are Maths/English marks not correlated, and this observed correlation emerged just by chance
This sounds like a Hypothesis Test!

transcription.tex: Test for positive correlation between English and Mathematics marks at the 10% significance level.
Paired marks and model summaries
One-tailed critical values. Columns 1–5 after the sample size give product moment values. The final three give Spearman values.
\(H_0:\rho=0\). There is no underlying linear correlation between the two marks.
\(H_1:\rho>0\). The alternative is positive linear correlation.
The table contains 10 paired marks, so \(n=10\).
Use the product moment column for a one-tailed test at 0.10. In the row for \(n=10\), the critical value is 0.4428.

The sample correlation is \(r=0.219\). Since \(0.219<0.4428\), do not reject \(H_0\).\par At the 10% significance level, there is insufficient evidence of positive linear correlation between English and Mathematics marks.
The critical value is the minimum correlation needed for rejection. Compare the numbers and state the conclusion in context.

transcription.tex: Question 3

a State what is measured by the product moment correlation coefficient. (1 mark) Twelve students sat two Biology tests, one theoretical the other practical. Their marks are shown below. \par $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline t&5&9&7&11&20&4&6&17&12&10&15&16\\\hline p&6&8&9&13&20&9&8&17&14&8&17&18\\\hline\end{array}$\par $t$: Marks in theoretical test. $p$: Marks in practical test.\par (b) Find the product moment correlation coefficient for these data, correct to 3 significant figures. (2 marks) A teacher claims that students who do well in their theoretical test also tend to do well in their practical test.\par (c) Test this claim at a 0.05 significance level, stating your hypotheses clearly. (3 marks)\par (d) Give an interpretation of the value 0.05 in your hypothesis test. (1 mark)
(a) It measures the direction and strength of linear correlation between two variables.
(b) The calculator gives \(r=0.935\).

(c) \(H_0:\rho=0\), \(H_1:\rho>0\); one tail, \(\alpha=0.05\).\par \(r=0.935>0.4973\), so reject \(H_0\). The marks show evidence of positive correlation. Students who score highly in the theoretical test tend to score highly in the practical test.
(d) If there is no population correlation, the test has a 5% probability of rejecting the null hypothesis.
Question 4

The following table shows the marks attained by 8 students in English and Mathematics tests. \par $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline Student&A&B&C&D&E&F&G&H\\\hline English&25&18&32&27&21&35&28&30\\\hline Mathematics&16&11&20&17&15&26&32&20\\\hline\end{array}$\par (a) Calculate the product moment correlation coefficient. (1 mark)\par (b) Test, at the 5% significance level, whether these results show evidence of a linear relationship between English and Mathematics marks. State your hypotheses clearly. (3 marks)
(a) \(r=0.68556\ldots\approx0.686\) (3 s.f.). Use the calculator’s correlation function.

(b) \(H_0:\rho=0\), \(H_1:\rho\ne0\).\par Either direction is possible. With \(n=8\), the two-tailed 5% critical value is \(0.7067\).\par \(|r|<0.7067\), so do not reject \(H_0\). There is insufficient evidence of a linear relationship between English and Mathematics marks.
Question 6

A scientific researcher collects data on the amount of solvent in a solution and the rate of reaction. She calculates the product moment correlation coefficient between the two sets of data and finds it to be -0.43. Given that she collected data from 15 samples, test, at the 5% level of significance, the claim that there is a negative correlation between the amount of solvent and the rate of reaction. State your hypotheses clearly. (3 marks)

\(H_0:\rho=0\), \(H_1:\rho<0\).\par The critical value is \(-0.4409\). Since \(-0.43>-0.4409\), do not reject \(H_0\). There is insufficient evidence of negative correlation between solvent amount and reaction rate.
Question 9

An employee at a weather centre believes that there is a negative correlation between humidity and visibility. She takes a sample of data from Heathrow in August 1987. \par $\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \mathrm{Humidity}\,(\%)&92&93&91&82&91&100\\\hline \mathrm{Visibility}\,(m)&2500&1500&2700&2900&2200&1000\\\hline\end{array}$\par © Crown Copyright Met Office\par (a) Calculate the product moment correlation coefficient for these data. (1 mark)\par (b) Test, at the 1% level of significance, the employee's claim. State your hypotheses clearly. (3 marks)

(b) \(H_0:\rho=0\), \(H_1:\rho<0\).\par The critical value is \(-0.8822\). Since \(-0.846>-0.8822\), do not reject \(H_0\). There is insufficient evidence of negative correlation between humidity and visibility.
